title: Procedural Dungeon Crawler
author: WanderingAdventure
selftext:
The Link provided has a Demo of a everything procedurally generated rogue lite game including enemies, bosses, the player, and each dungeon. I built a tool to dynamically create these things just based off config (JSON) and then from this i can procedurally generate different enemies, bosses, and assets in general. I can even do human/animal shapes and all sorts of cool stuff. This was built in 2 days with the help of my boy Claude so still a bit rough around the edges. But AI Has been absolutely instrumental in getting this to where it is. I find AI can be very intelligent when it comes to pathing and generation if you guide it properly. Where i still think AI is lacking is fluidity of asset generation even if its procedural you have to guide it with images of references and make it stay on track and keep iterating.

Would love some feedback to see people's thoughts or areas of improvement. 

It's a threejs game but I also have a version that I'm going to be throwing on steam soon. Making a web version is great for validation of an idea.

Link here: [https://aspectdigitalsoftware.com/games/dungeoncrawler](https://aspectdigitalsoftware.com/games/dungeoncrawler)

comments.author: Own_Principle_7901
comments.body: Felt good to play, but becomes repetitive really fast.

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body: Any suggestions on what should get improved on, maybe some puzzles or a room that locks until you do something? something like that i think could make it more interesting

replies.author: Own_Principle_7901
replies.body: What about lore, a reason to go for a dungeon? Ever incresing dungeon sizes with different levels of enemies? Some kind of grinding? What about permanment buffs, optional dungeons?

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body:
You earn shards at the end of a run where you can buy armor and weapon upgrades that are actually procedurally generated onto the player so everyone’s character will look totally different. As for the grinding I have some ideas. 

With regards to the optional dungeons what are you thinking for that? Technically each dungeon is its own seed. I could do high scores on a per dungeon level or have set dungeons.

Let me cook on the puzzles I think it will add a little extra to this game.

replies.author: Own_Principle_7901
replies.body:
I'm not a high scoring player, I'm more of an explorer player. When I play a game, I want to feel I can do more than just walking foward while watching my character hit the enemies. I want to go to a room and see a lore piece. I want to go to a dungeon a accomplish a quest. I want to go to a dungeon that it was not required me to go, but it was there and the reward was a funny hat. 

And the "Reward Cards" mechanic are overused and anti-player. MY OPINION, but your game don't need it. Vampire Survivor + Dungeon Crawler is not a good match, BUT you made a very nice framework a dungeon crawler.

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body:
Ya reward cards are not great, but it is a simple way for progression. The puzzles i am about to release are actually pretty fun there's 3 distinct puzzles at the moment, but i'll add some more. I'm also introducing lore in the form of runes you discover on walls. Each rune gives you a bit more knowledge of the why and what. 

What might be interesting is allowing my procedural system to come up with what these cards do, and their effects are maybe hidden to the player until they uncover certain runes too. A neat twist on the issue with "Reward Level Up Cards"

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body:
Ok released some new stuff if you don’t mind trying it out more.

\- added 3 different puzzles (approx 2-3 will show up in a dungeon)  
\- cards are hidden with ??? Until you discover the glyphs  
\- glyphs have some lore behind them

Gunna look into maybe a different combat system other than auto fire.

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body: Adding puzzles now will be on the next build in 45 min

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body:
Its a good start but turn off the auto fire. It makes it entirely too easy. Have the firig be a point and click.

Also I would tell the user where they are going to the have a goal in mind as they explore the dungeon.

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body: You can also use point and click for movement but I’m going to try something to improve combat and make it feel not as easy. Let me cook here.

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body:
Added an option for manual attacking it allows for a more aim style approach to combat. 

On keyboard holding SHIFT keeps you planted and allows you to click and shoot in the direction you want, on mobile two finger tap keeps you still then you can move around aiming to shoot

On mobile i recommend the auto aim just because it feels more natural, but on desktop its actually not a bad combat mechanic and allows for some interesting play. This does mean that SHIFT no longer does the dash but space will do the dash.

(NOTE: on mobile you can dash by double tapping in the direction you are tapping)

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body: I just added a way to not do the auto shoot but a way to stand in place and aim where you want to shoot (another comment i mention how the controls for this work). I'll remove the pushing crate minigame i feel like it dampers gameplay a bit, i still like the other minigames like simon says, and the getting locked in and facing a few waves. comments.author: PanicPengu
comments.body:
Just a heads up that I got stuck in one of the runic pattern rooms and quit playing because it was bugged. Maybe put in something so that if you're puzzle room is broken it's not just a prison.

Also I didn't really feel like either of the puzzle rooms I was in added anything to the game.

Some kind of controls help in game so that you know what the controls are and can switch from auto fire.

replies.author: WanderingAdventure
replies.body:
Great feedback I think im going to remove the simon says puzzle, i removed the box puzzle too but i'll keep the one where you fight a couple waves before you can leave. 

If you go to settings on the main menu you can switch from auto fire to aim and shoot. It's not great on mobile but on desktop it feels good.
